coordinates.note: Campus-grade point from OpenStreetMap geocoding of the Kamioka mine (a node labelled Kamioka Mine / ICRR / Kamiokande); the position of lab-D inside the mine is not published in the sources read.

depth_mwe.note: A December 2023 collaboration talk gives '1000 m.w.e.' for the Kamioka laboratory; the 2020 paper's 2700 m.w.e. is used.
depth_mwe.quote: The current setup of the detector system, which is called CANDLES-III, is installed at lab-D of the Kamioka Underground Laboratory (2700 m.w.e.) in the Institute of Cosmic Ray Research of the University of Tokyo.

summary.plain: Laboratory lab-D inside the Kamioka mine in Gifu, Japan, 2700 metres of water-equivalent below the surface, where the CANDLES calcium-fluoride detector runs.
summary.technical: Lab-D of the Kamioka Underground Laboratory (ICRR, University of Tokyo), 2700 m.w.e.; marked with a campus-grade point for the Kamioka mine.
